sights.address: 16701 Collins Ave, Sunny Isles Beach, FL
sights.w: 600-foot Atlantic fishing pier behind Pier Park — sunrise strolls, anglers and the condo-tower skyline.

sights.address: Collins Ave, Sunny Isles Beach, FL
sights.w: Miles of wide golden beach under the 'Florida Riviera' condo towers between Haulover and Golden Beach.
One of America's largest malls, with a public art programme — Carsten Höller's 93-ft spiral Aventura Slide Tower is a rideable sculpture.

sights.n: Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts
sights.w: Miami's $500M César Pelli performing-arts centre — Broadway, opera, ballet and the Art Deco Sears tower preserved on its plaza.
Bayfront home arena of the Miami Heat and the city's big-concert stage.
Free elevated people-mover with 21 stations — the best (and cheapest) skyline ride through downtown and Brickell.
Small man-made island off Brickell with a waterfront perimeter path — the neighbourhood's quiet escape.

sights.address: Under the Metrorail, Brickell, Miami, FL
sights.w: Linear park and trail being built beneath the Metrorail — the Brickell Backyard section has gyms, gardens and the Oolite Room.

sights.n: Broward Center for the Performing Arts
sights.w: Riverfront performing-arts centre on the New River — Broadway tours, opera and the Riverwalk arts district anchor.

sights.n: Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino (Guitar Hotel)
sights.w: The Seminole Tribe's 450-foot guitar-shaped hotel tower, casino and Hard Rock Live arena — Broward's most improbable landmark.
Sternwheeler sightseeing cruises up the New River since 1935 — 'Venice of America' mansions from the water.
Broward's north-end beach with the International Fishing Pier and a laid-back boardwalk.
Wide beach with the rebuilt Fisher Family Pier and some of Broward's best shore diving and fishing.
Quiet barrier-island beach beneath the 1907 Hillsboro Inlet lighthouse, one of the most powerful on the East Coast.
Old-Florida beach town with a fishing pier and quiet sand between Port Everglades and Hollywood.
Broward's southernmost beach, a calm stretch at the Miami-Dade line.
A 1920s industrial bakery turned (since 1985) into ~100 artists' studios and galleries — open studios show Wynwood before the murals.
Main Everglades entrance visitor centre — exhibits, orientation film, and the start of the 38-mile road to Flamingo; open 365 days.

sights.address: Everglades National Park (Long Pine Key area), FL
sights.w: Cold War Nike Hercules 'Alpha Battery' frozen since 1979 — barracks, missile barns and a real missile; ranger-led tours in season.

sights.address: Main Park Rd, Everglades National Park, FL
sights.w: Half-mile boardwalk through a hardwood hammock to the largest living mahogany tree in the US.

sights.address: Royal Palm, Everglades National Park, FL
sights.w: Shaded, jungle-like paved loop through a hardwood hammock beside the Anhinga Trail at Royal Palm.

sights.address: Main Park Rd, Everglades National Park, FL
sights.w: 5.2-mile paddling loop through sawgrass marsh and mangrove islands — gators, crocodiles, snail kites; guided canoe trips.

sights.address: Main Park Rd, Everglades National Park, FL
sights.w: Mangrove boardwalk on West Lake and the trailhead for an 8-mile paddle of open lakes to Alligator Creek — crocodile country.

sights.address: 815 Oyster Bar Ln, Everglades City, FL
sights.w: The park's western gateway — boat tours into the Ten Thousand Islands mangrove maze and backcountry paddling routes.
Largest island of Biscayne NP — a former pioneer pineapple-farming and sponging community; camping, a loop trail, bayside picnics (check NPS for current access).
Day-use island on swift Caesar Creek with a short hardwood-hammock trail, picnic pavilion and dawn-to-dusk access.

sights.address: Tamiami Trail & Turner River Rd, Ochopee, FL
sights.w: 200-m boardwalk over a cypress waterway packed with gators, turtles and wading birds — the gateway to Turner River Road.

sights.address: Turner River Rd (CR 839), Big Cypress National Preserve, FL
sights.w: 17-mile gravel loop through wet prairies and cypress — one of South Florida's best drive-up gator and wading-bird routes.

sights.address: Ocean Dr, 5th–15th St, Miami Beach, FL
sights.w: The classic South Beach strand in front of Ocean Drive's Art Deco row — lifeguard towers, volleyball, the people-watching beach.

sights.address: Collins Ave, 60th–87th St, Miami Beach, FL
sights.w: The calmer, locals' end of Miami Beach with North Beach Oceanside Park and a MiMo-era hotel strip.
Sleepy residential beach town under a mile long — small-town vibes between North Beach and Bal Harbour.
Manicured beach and jogging path fronting Bal Harbour's resorts; the Bal Harbour Shops are across Collins.

sights.n: The Fillmore Miami Beach (Jackie Gleason Theater)
sights.w: 1950s theatre where Jackie Gleason taped his TV show, now a Live Nation concert hall.
1961 MiMo open-air bandshell in North Beach — free and cheap concerts, Afro-Caribbean nights and film screenings.
Sidewalk stars honouring Latin stars from Celia Cruz to Gloria Estefan along Calle Ocho.
1917 stilt-built trading post and post office at the end of the road on Chokoloskee — now a museum of frontier and Seminole trade (NRHP).
Collier County museum in the 1927 Everglades Laundry — Calusa, Seminole, pioneer and Barron Collier history of the southwest Glades.

sights.address: Tamiami Trail (US 41), ~40 mi west of Miami, FL
sights.w: The Miccosukee Tribe's village on the Tamiami Trail reservation — living-history museum, crafts, alligator demonstrations and airboat rides.
Rebuilt (2026) 2,000-ft boardwalk into a virgin cypress strand spared from logging — ghost-orchid country in Fakahatchee Strand Preserve State Park.
Home of Dana A. Dorsey, Florida's first Black millionaire, who built Overtown one rental house per parcel — NRHP-listed (1989).
